newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal says won't present candidate for U.N. job.
newsitem.headline: Senegal says won't present candidate for U.N. job.

text.p: Senegal said on Tuesday it had decided not to present Foreign Minister Moustapha Niasse as a candidate to succeed U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali.

"We are witnessing a proliferation of candidates from different African countries. Senegal, in the spirit of dynamic compromise, has made it known that it has decided not to present the candidature of minister of state Moustapha Niasse at this stage," a government statement said after a cabinet meeting.
President Abdou Diouf announced his intention to propose Niasse in remarks to reporters last Friday on his return from a Franco-African summit in Burkina Faso.
"I see in him the profile of a secretary-general of the United Nations and I have given my endorsement," he said.
But Senegal's recognition of Taiwan meant his candidature would have been inevitably vetoed by China which regards Taiwan as a rebel province. Beijing broke ties with Dakar in January.
The Security Council was due late on Tuesday to hold informal balloting to test the popularity of four declared candidates.

The four declared candidates are Kofi Annan of Ghana, the U.N. undersecretary-general for peacekeeping operations; Hamid Algabid of Niger, secretary-general of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference; Amara Essy, foreign minister of the Ivory Coast; and Ahmedou Ould-Abdallah of Mauritania, a former U.N. special envoy for Burundi who now heads the Washington-based Global Coalition for Africa.
Several other potential African candidates have been the subject of speculation, including Salim Ahmed Salim, the secretary-general of the Organisation of African Unity.
